title: A Choir for the Veil
premise: In the valley of Vell, magic cannot cross the border stones, which is why Casper Ishikawa — a thief who steals memories with her hands — has never left. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted and her stolen memories begin to whisper of a king bound to something ancient wearing his face, Casper is dragged out of the valley by hunters who need her gift to unbind him. She must choose between loyalty to the mentor who taught her to steal and the truth that he helped bind the king in the first place. In the end, she unbinds King Aldric by returning every memory she has ever stolen — including her own childhood — and the veil between valley and world falls, letting magic in at last.
about_author: Theo Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. They write fantasy about inheritance, small betrayals, and the things we keep locked in attics.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. We meet Casper mid-heist, lifting a dying woman's happiest memory for a client who pays in bread. The valley's border stones hum at the edge of town, and magic cannot follow anyone past them. Emotional beat: cozy competence shadowed by loneliness — Casper owns hundreds of memories but none are hers.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Well
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A royal herald announces the hunt: all gifted persons must surrender themselves or be taken. That night, hunters arrive asking about a thief whose victims wake with gaps in their lives. Casper's mentor, Odell, lies smoothly for her — too smoothly. Emotional beat: dread arriving dressed as routine.

chapters.title: What Odell Kept
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, ending on Odell's. Searching Odell's cellar for escape routes, Casper finds a stolen royal memory sealed in glass: a young King Aldric binding himself to something beneath the mountain. Odell catches her holding it. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold draft — the man who raised her is complicit in the hunt.

chapters.title: Taken Across the Stones
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hunters seize them both; crossing the border, magic floods back into Casper's body like water into a lung, and her gift sharpens painfully. In the capital's dungeons she meets Sera, a hunter who secretly doubts the crown. Emotional beat: disorientation and awe — the world outside is larger and crueler than promised.

chapters.title: The Court of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera escorts Casper through court, where nobles smile with rehearsed warmth and the king hasn't been seen unmasked in a year. Sera reveals she was ordered to deliver Casper not to justice but to the throne room. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two women used as tools.

chapters.title: An Audience with Winter
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Brought before Aldric, Casper touches his hand and glimpses the truth: the thing wearing the crown is feeding on his memories, and its hunger is summoning an early, endless winter. It offers her a bargain — serve it, and Odell goes free. Emotional beat: terror braided with temptation.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Confession
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. Imprisoned nearby, Odell recalls binding Aldric decades ago to stop a war, believing sacrifice was mercy. He confesses to Casper through the cell wall and gives her the one thing that can undo it: the counter-ritual, which requires returning every stolen memory to its owner. Emotional beat: grief and forgiveness entangled.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The false king seals the city; snow falls in summer and the hunt becomes a purge. Sera chooses treason, breaking Casper out, and they gather the glass-sealed memories from the crown vault while the court sleeps under enchanted frost. Emotional beat: loyalty crystallizing into open rebellion.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the throne room, Casper begins the return — pressing memory after memory back into Aldric, each one weakening the thing beneath the crown. It fights with her own stolen childhood, showing her why she was left in the valley. She returns that too. Emotional beat: climax as self-sacrifice; the cost is her last anchor to herself.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Veil
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, closing with Sera's. Aldric wakes whole; the entity dissolves into the first true spring thaw, and the border stones crack — magic flows freely now. Memoryless but alive, Casper stays in the capital, where Sera and the people she once robbed begin giving her new memories freely. Emotional beat: belonging earned not by taking, but by giving everything back.
